author: The Infographics Show
description:
Deep beneath Chernobyl’s Reactor 4 lies Room 305/2, an almost inaccessible chamber containing some of the most dangerous radioactive material on Earth. Decades after the 1986 nuclear disaster, scientists detected something unexpected inside the reactor ruins. Rising neutron counts. In one area, the readings roughly doubled over several years, raising questions about what is happening inside the hardened remains of the melted nuclear fuel.

This video explores why Chernobyl is still dangerous, how the massive New Safe Confinement was designed to contain its radioactive debris, and why sealing the reactor may have changed conditions inside it in ways scientists didn’t fully anticipate.
We also examine the challenges of sending robots into radiation-filled environments, the damage caused to Chernobyl’s protective structure in 2025, and the mysterious fungi that appear to thrive in radioactive surroundings.
